checks: A finite nonnegative concave function on a finite interval is bounded above by interior continuity and extrapolation from fixed interior points toward either end. Positivity on the interior gives ℓ(0)=L. Combining strict superlevel intervals by Minkowski interpolation proves concavity of their lengths.
The lower chord from height zero to levels tending to H yields U≥LH^m/(m+1), even when H is not attained on an open interval. Thus c≥H and the comparison profile is affine up to H.

The concavity of g=ℓ−ℓ₀ before H and g(0)=0 imply that g(s)/s is nonincreasing. The extension has g≤0 after H and allows a plateau jump. Equal m-moment and multiplication by s^(p−m)−s₀^(p−m) preserve the correct sign for p<m; integrability at zero follows because p≥1 and profiles are bounded.

The p=m case is an identity. A nondegenerate tent or a one-sided affine function has the indicated linear superlevel-length profile, hence gives equality. Source b69ebda3a2e6d72a §2 (1) gives the same coefficient and proof.
readability: The stated hypotheses and proof scope are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The one-crossing superlevel argument proves the sharp normalized moment inequality, including plateau maxima and both equality examples.
